questions.q:
Consider the following statements about greenhouse gases:
1. Methane has a longer atmospheric lifetime than carbon dioxide.
2. Sulphur hexafluoride has the highest global warming potential among CO2, CH4, N2O and SF6.
3. Nitrous oxide emissions arise largely from agricultural soils and nitrogen fertiliser use.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Methane lasts only about a dozen years in the air against centuries for the effective persistence of CO2, but it traps far more heat per tonne in the short run. SF6, used in electrical equipment, is thousands of times more potent than CO2 per tonne.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Carbon dioxide
2. Methane
3. Sulphur hexafluoride
4. Water vapour
How many of the above are greenhouse gases covered by the Kyoto Protocol?
questions.e: The Kyoto basket has six gases: CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs and SF6 (NF3 was added later). Water vapour is a natural greenhouse gas whose amount responds to temperature, so it is not regulated.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change
questions.h: Kyoto basket = 6 gases, water vapour not one.

questions.q: In the absence of the natural greenhouse effect, the average surface temperature of the Earth would be approximately
questions.e: With the natural greenhouse effect, the average is around 15 degrees Celsius. Without it, Earth would average roughly -18 degrees, a difference of about 33 degrees.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Greenhouse gases warm the lower atmosphere even though they are largely transparent to incoming solar radiation.
Statement-II: Greenhouse gases absorb and re-radiate the outgoing long-wave infrared radiation emitted by the Earth's surface.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Sunlight (mostly short-wave) passes through, warms the surface, and the surface sends back long-wave heat. Greenhouse gases intercept this heat and send part of it back down, which is what keeps the lower atmosphere warm.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about radiative forcing:
1. Radiative forcing is the change in the net energy balance of the Earth system caused by a driver such as a change in greenhouse gas concentration.
2. Sulphate aerosols have a net positive radiative forcing.
3. Black carbon has a warming influence because it absorbs sunlight.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Sulphate aerosols reflect sunlight and have a net cooling (negative) forcing, partly offsetting greenhouse warming. Black carbon absorbs sunlight and warms the air and darkens snow.

questions.q: Climate is conventionally defined as the statistical description of weather averaged over a period of
questions.e: The World Meteorological Organization uses 30-year averages, called climate normals, to separate climate from year-to-year weather variability.

questions.q:
How many of the following are positive feedbacks that amplify global warming?
1. Melting of sea ice that exposes darker ocean water
2. Thawing of permafrost that releases methane and carbon dioxide
3. Increased carbon uptake by plants growing faster under higher CO2
4. Dieback of forests that releases stored carbon
questions.e: Melting ice lowers albedo, permafrost thaw adds greenhouse gases and forest dieback adds carbon, each reinforcing warming. Faster plant growth removes carbon dioxide, a negative (damping) feedback.
questions.h: Positive = Pushes it further; negative = Nudges it back.

questions.q:
Climate scientists have identified several tipping elements in the Earth system. How many of the following are generally considered potential tipping elements?
1. Greenland ice sheet
2. Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation
3. Amazon rainforest
4. Warm-water coral reefs
questions.e: Each of these could shift abruptly into a new state if warming passes a threshold, and the change would be hard to reverse over human timescales.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Large explosive volcanic eruptions can temporarily cool the global climate.
Statement-II: Sulphate aerosols injected into the stratosphere reflect part of the incoming solar radiation.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: The 1991 Mount Pinatubo eruption cooled the Earth by a fraction of a degree for a couple of years. Stratospheric aerosols persist long enough to affect the global radiation balance, unlike tropospheric aerosols which wash out quickly.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC):
1. It was established by the UNFCCC in 1992.
2. Its Working Group II assesses impacts, adaptation and vulnerability.
3. It shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 2007.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The IPCC was set up in 1988 by the World Meteorological Organization and UNEP, before the UNFCCC existed. It does not do its own research but assesses published science.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the IPCC Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 degrees Celsius (2018):
1. It was prepared on the invitation of the UNFCCC made at the Paris conference.
2. It found that limiting warming to 1.5 degrees would require global net anthropogenic CO2 emissions to fall by about 45 percent from 2010 levels by 2030, reaching net zero around 2050.
3. It concluded that limiting warming to 1.5 degrees would need no major changes in energy systems.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Staying at 1.5 degrees demands rapid and far-reaching transitions in energy, land, industry, buildings and transport; the report said so explicitly.

questions.q: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, adopted at the Earth Summit in 1992, entered into force in
questions.e: The Convention entered into force in March 1994 after 50 ratifications. 1997 was the year of the Kyoto Protocol, and the Protocol itself entered into force in 2005.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q: Which one of the following UNFCCC Annexes lists the developed countries that are obliged to provide financial resources to developing countries?
questions.e: Annex I contains industrialised countries and economies in transition; Annex II is the subset of OECD members, which carry the financing and technology-transfer obligations. Annex B belongs to the Kyoto Protocol.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Kyoto Protocol:
1. It set legally binding emission targets only for developed (Annex I) countries.
2. Its first commitment period (2008-2012) required Annex I countries to cut emissions by about 10 percent below 1990 levels on average.
3. It established the flexibility mechanisms of Emissions Trading, Joint Implementation and the Clean Development Mechanism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The average cut was about 5 percent below 1990 levels, not 10. The Protocol rests on the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities, which is why developing countries such as India and China had no binding targets.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q: The second commitment period of the Kyoto Protocol, agreed under the Doha Amendment, covers the years
questions.e: The Doha Amendment (2012) extended Kyoto for 2013-2020, but only a limited set of developed countries took on targets in it. It bridged the gap until the Paris Agreement took over from 2020.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Paris Agreement (2015):
1. It aims to hold the global average temperature rise well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels and to pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5 degrees.
2. It provides for a global stocktake every five years to assess collective progress.
3. It sets legally binding emission reduction targets for each developed country.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Parties must submit and pursue Nationally Determined Contributions, but the targets in them are self-determined and not legally binding. This 'bottom-up' design replaced Kyoto's 'top-down' targets.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 6 of the Paris Agreement:
1. Article 6.2 provides for a centralised mechanism supervised by a UN body to issue credits.
2. Article 6.4 establishes a mechanism, overseen by a supervisory body appointed under the Agreement, that is often regarded as the successor to the Clean Development Mechanism.
3. Article 6.8 deals with non-market approaches.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 6.2 is decentralised: countries trade 'internationally transferred mitigation outcomes' bilaterally. Article 6.4 is the UN-supervised, centralised crediting mechanism.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's updated Nationally Determined Contribution (August 2022):
1. It commits to reduce the emissions intensity of GDP by 45 percent by 2030 from the 2005 level.
2. It aims at about 50 percent cumulative electric power installed capacity from non-fossil fuel sources by 2030.
3. It commits India to net zero emissions by 2050.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India's net zero target is 2070, announced by the Prime Minister at Glasgow in 2021. The 2022 NDC converted part of that Panchamrit pledge into formal targets.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT among the 'Panchamrit' announcements made by India at COP26 in Glasgow?
o: Peak in national greenhouse gas emissions by 2030
500 GW of non-fossil fuel energy capacity by 2030
50 percent of energy requirements from renewable energy by 2030
questions.e: India's five commitments were 500 GW non-fossil capacity, 50 percent renewable energy, a cut of 1 billion tonnes in projected emissions by 2030, a 45 percent fall in carbon intensity, and net zero by 2070. India did not announce a peaking year.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the eight missions of India's National Action Plan on Climate Change (2008)?
o: National Mission for a Green India
questions.e: The eight missions cover solar energy, enhanced energy efficiency, sustainable habitat, water, sustaining the Himalayan ecosystem, a Green India, sustainable agriculture, and strategic knowledge for climate change. Wetland conservation has its own separate programme.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Fund/Body) with List-II (Feature):
List-I: A. Green Climate Fund  B. Adaptation Fund  C. Global Environment Facility  D. National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (India)
List-II: 1. Headquartered at Songdo, South Korea  2. Partly financed by a 2 percent share of proceeds of Clean Development Mechanism credits  3. Established in 1991 and serves as financial mechanism for several environmental conventions  4. NABARD is its National Implementing Entity
questions.e: The Adaptation Fund was set up under the Kyoto Protocol and gets a share of CDM proceeds. India's NAFCC, launched in 2015, channels adaptation money to State projects through NABARD.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q:
Match List-I (Greenhouse gas) with List-II (Typical source):
List-I: A. Methane  B. Nitrous oxide  C. Sulphur hexafluoride  D. Hydrofluorocarbons
List-II: 1. Flooded rice fields and ruminant digestion  2. Use of nitrogenous fertilisers in agriculture  3. Insulation in high-voltage electrical equipment  4. Refrigeration and air conditioning
questions.e: Methane comes from anaerobic decomposition (paddy fields, livestock, landfills), N2O from nitrogen applied to soils, SF6 from switchgear, and HFCs from cooling equipment.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Country/Bloc) with List-II (Declared net-zero or climate-neutrality target year):
List-I: A. India  B. European Union  C. Turkey  D. Saudi Arabia
List-II: 1. 2050  2. 2053  3. 2060  4. 2070
questions.e: India announced 2070 at COP26; the EU aims for climate neutrality by 2050; Turkey announced 2053 and Saudi Arabia 2060 in the run-up to Glasgow.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. COP3 (1997) : Kyoto Protocol adopted
2. COP16 (2010) : Green Climate Fund established
3. COP21 (2015) : Doha Amendment adopted
4. COP26 (2021) : Fund for loss and damage agreed
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Doha Amendment dates from COP18 (2012), and the loss-and-damage fund was agreed at COP27 in Sharm el-Sheikh in 2022. Pairs 1 and 2 are correct.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the chronological order of their adoption:
P. Paris Agreement
Q. Kyoto Protocol
R. Glasgow Climate Pact
S. Bali Action Plan
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Kyoto (1997), Bali (2007), Paris (2015), Glasgow (2021).
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The first Global Stocktake under the Paris Agreement was concluded at COP26 in Glasgow.
2. COP28 in Dubai called for transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems.
3. COP29 in Baku set a new collective quantified goal for finance, with developed countries to take the lead in mobilising at least 300 billion US dollars a year by 2035.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The first Global Stocktake concluded at COP28 in 2023, as the Agreement requires a stocktake every five years starting in 2023. COP26 was a year of pledges, not the stocktake.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q: The Glasgow Climate Pact (COP26) was the first UNFCCC decision to explicitly refer to coal. After a last-minute change sought by India, the wording on coal became
questions.e: The original text said 'phase-out'. India and others objected, arguing for developing-country space, and the final text read 'phase-down of unabated coal power', along with phase-out of inefficient fossil fuel subsidies.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Global Methane Pledge:
1. It was launched at the Paris climate conference in 2015.
2. It seeks to reduce global anthropogenic methane emissions by at least 30 percent below 2020 levels by 2030.
3. Methane is a short-lived climate pollutant, so cutting it can quickly slow near-term warming.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Pledge was launched at COP26 in Glasgow in 2021 by the United States and the European Union. Because methane lasts about a decade, cuts show up in warming within a few years.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q:
Statement-I: Methane has a higher global warming potential than carbon dioxide over a 100-year horizon.
Statement-II: Methane remains in the atmosphere for a longer time than carbon dioxide.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Methane absorbs far more heat per molecule, giving it a higher GWP, but it breaks down in about a dozen years whereas a large part of emitted CO2 stays for centuries.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Deposition of black carbon on Himalayan glaciers slows their melting.
Statement-II: Dark soot particles absorb more solar radiation and reduce the albedo of snow and ice.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Soot darkens the surface, so snow absorbs more sunlight and melts faster. That lower albedo is why black carbon is a concern for Himalayan glaciers and snowpack.

questions.q: Which one of the following paddy cultivation practices helps reduce methane emissions?
o: Continuous flooding throughout the crop season
Incorporation of large amounts of fresh organic manure into standing water
Alternate wetting and drying of the field
questions.e: Methane is made by methanogenic bacteria in waterlogged, oxygen-free soil. Draining the field periodically lets air in and interrupts methane production; methods such as SRI and direct-seeded rice work on the same principle.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about ocean acidification:
1. Dissolved atmospheric carbon dioxide forms carbonic acid and lowers the pH of seawater.
2. It reduces the availability of carbonate ions needed by corals and shell-forming organisms.
3. It is caused mainly by rising ocean temperature rather than by absorbed carbon dioxide.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The oceans take up a large share of human CO2 emissions, so their average surface pH has dropped by about 0.1 unit since pre-industrial times. Warming is a separate stress, not the cause of acidification.

questions.q: Coral bleaching under thermal stress is caused primarily by
o: expulsion of symbiotic zooxanthellae algae from coral tissue
death of coral polyps through a loss of calcium
excessive growth of algae smothering the coral
a sudden rise in salinity of the sea
questions.e: Corals get colour and much of their food from zooxanthellae. Heat stress makes the corals expel them, leaving the white skeleton visible and the coral starved. Prolonged bleaching kills the coral.

questions.q: Which one of the following does NOT significantly contribute to global mean sea-level rise?
o: Melting of the Greenland ice sheet
Melting of floating Arctic sea ice
questions.e: Floating ice already displaces its own weight of water, so melting changes sea level only negligibly (like ice in a glass). Ice that sits on land, and the expansion of warming water, add volume.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ahmedabad was the first city in South Asia to develop a Heat Action Plan, in 2013.
2. The Hindu Kush Himalaya is sometimes called the Third Pole because it holds the largest store of ice outside the polar regions.
3. The International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) is headquartered in Thimphu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: ICIMOD is headquartered in Kathmandu, Nepal, and serves eight regional member countries of the Hindu Kush Himalaya.

questions.q:
How many of the following are geological formations considered suitable for carbon dioxide storage in carbon capture and storage projects?
1. Depleted oil and gas reservoirs
2. Deep saline aquifers
3. Unmineable coal seams
4. Basalt rock formations in which CO2 mineralises into carbonate
questions.e: All four are being used or tested. In basalt, as in Iceland's CarbFix project, injected CO2 reacts with the rock and turns into solid carbonate within a few years.

questions.q:
How many of the following are carbon dioxide removal approaches, rather than solar radiation management?
1. Afforestation
2. Stratospheric aerosol injection
3. Marine cloud brightening
4. Direct air capture with storage
questions.e: CDR takes CO2 out of the air (afforestation, direct air capture). Stratospheric aerosols and marine cloud brightening only reflect sunlight, leaving the CO2 in place and the ocean acidification unaffected.

questions.q: India submitted its Long-Term Low-Carbon Development Strategy to the UNFCCC in
questions.e: India submitted the strategy at COP27 in Sharm el-Sheikh (November 2022), as required of parties under the Paris Agreement, and tied it to the 2070 net-zero goal and Mission LiFE.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about carbon pricing:
1. Under a carbon tax, the regulator fixes the quantity of emissions and the price is set by the market.
2. Under a cap-and-trade system, the regulator fixes the total quantity of emissions and the price of allowances is set by the market.
3. A carbon credit typically represents one tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent reduced or removed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A tax fixes the price and leaves the quantity of emissions uncertain; a cap fixes the quantity and lets the price float. The EU Emissions Trading System, launched in 2005, is the best known cap-and-trade scheme.
questions.h: Tax = fixes Price; Cap = fixes Quantity.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's carbon market:
1. The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme was notified in 2023 under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 as amended in 2022.
2. The Bureau of Energy Efficiency is the administrator of the scheme.
3. Under the Perform, Achieve and Trade scheme, over-achievers receive Renewable Energy Certificates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PAT over-achievers get Energy Saving Certificates (ESCerts), which are tradable; Renewable Energy Certificates belong to the separate RE certificate market.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM):
1. It is a carbon tax imposed by the World Trade Organization on developing countries.
2. It covers imports of goods such as iron and steel, cement, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen.
3. It is meant to equalise the carbon price paid on imports with that paid by EU producers, preventing carbon leakage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: CBAM is an EU instrument, not a WTO one. After a transitional reporting phase that began in October 2023, the definitive phase started in 2026, requiring importers to buy certificates.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Green Credit Programme of India:
1. It was launched by the Ministry of Power.
2. It is administered by the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education.
3. It covers voluntary environmental actions such as water conservation, waste management and mangrove protection in addition to tree plantation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Programme was notified in 2023 by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change as a market-based incentive for voluntary environmental actions, not by the Ministry of Power.

questions.q: Under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, India's target for annual green hydrogen production capacity by 2030 is
questions.e: The Mission aims at about 5 million metric tonnes of green hydrogen per year by 2030, with associated renewable energy capacity addition, to help decarbonise fertiliser, refining and steel.

questions.q: The '4 per 1000' initiative, launched at the Paris climate conference, aims to
o: increase soil organic carbon stocks by 0.4 percent a year
cut methane emissions by 4 percent every thousand days
plant four trees per thousand people
limit the global temperature rise to 0.4 degrees
questions.e: Raising soil carbon by 0.4 percent a year could, in principle, offset a large part of annual anthropogenic CO2 emissions while improving soil fertility.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Initiative) with List-II (Where/when it was launched):
List-I: A. International Solar Alliance  B. Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure  C. Global Biofuels Alliance  D. Global Methane Pledge
List-II: 1. COP21, Paris, 2015  2. UN Climate Action Summit, New York, 2019  3. G20 Summit, New Delhi, 2023  4. COP26, Glasgow, 2021
questions.e: India co-led the ISA, CDRI and the Global Biofuels Alliance; the Global Methane Pledge was a US-EU initiative.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Milankovitch cycles:
1. Eccentricity refers to the change in the shape of the Earth's orbit around the Sun.
2. Obliquity refers to the change in the shape of the Earth's orbit.
3. The tilt of the Earth's axis varies between about 22.1 and 24.5 degrees over a cycle of roughly 41,000 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Obliquity is the tilt of the axis. Together with eccentricity and precession (the wobble of the axis), these slow orbital changes pace the glacial and interglacial periods, but cannot explain the rapid warming since the 1950s.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of reports and publishers:
1. Emissions Gap Report : United Nations Environment Programme
2. Global Climate Risk Index : Germanwatch
3. State of the Global Climate : World Meteorological Organization
4. Climate Change Performance Index : Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Climate Change Performance Index is published by Germanwatch with the NewClimate Institute and Climate Action Network. The IPCC publishes assessment reports, not rankings.

questions.q:
Statement-I: According to the World Meteorological Organization and Copernicus, 2024 was the first calendar year in which the global mean temperature exceeded 1.5 degrees Celsius above the 1850-1900 level.
Statement-II: The Paris Agreement's long-term temperature goal is assessed over multi-decade averages, so a single year above 1.5 degrees does not by itself mean that the goal has been breached.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: A strong El Nino added to long-term warming in 2024. The Paris goal refers to the long-term average, normally taken as 20 years, so one hot year is a warning, not a formal breach.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change

questions.q: Blue carbon ecosystems such as mangroves, seagrass meadows and salt marshes store the largest share of their carbon in
o: the soil and sediments beneath them
questions.e: Waterlogged, oxygen-poor sediments slow decomposition, so carbon can remain locked for centuries. Draining or clearing these ecosystems releases it, turning a sink into a source.

questions.q: The fund for responding to loss and damage in vulnerable developing countries was agreed at the climate conference held at
questions.e: COP27 (2022) agreed to set up the fund after years of pressure from vulnerable countries, building on the Warsaw International Mechanism of 2013. COP28 in Dubai operationalised it.
questions.s: UNFCCC / Shankar IAS Environment, Climate Change
